findings.text: V1's cursors don't move. They get drawn into every tracked piece and never go away. `Widget.js:304` sets `track` on every live owner line, and `Chat.js` `tracked_text_node()` gives each one its own ✓ and 🧠. So a bubble of five sentences ends up with five standing pairs. The brief (`v1-cursors-brief.md` 1–3) asks for ONE ✓ after the newest fast chunk and ONE 🧠 after the newest sentence, moved the way v2's `place_cursors()` moves them. Ask 2 also asks for "a mark only when pending or wrong". The `chat-sent.mjs:426` check (`sentText.length === 2`) only passes because that test sends a single line.

When no sentence in a piece has finished yet, the 🧠 is drawn in front of the text. `last_finished_sentence_end()` returns 0 in that case, and `tracked_text_node()` still appends the brain at offset 0. So "so, it works" draws as "🧠so, it works ✓". The brain should be left out (or kept on the previous piece) until a sentence ends. `chunks.test.mjs` only checks the 0; it never checks what gets drawn.

The V1 merge rule goes against the owner's rule in `open-bubble-last-brief.md`: "Once the Prompt is closed (a new Prompt starts), it stays where it is". It also goes against ask 11 ("a spoken Prompt closes ... on an assistant reply"). `mergeable()` keys on sender plus the 8 s gap, never on the Prompt. The rewritten `chat-sent.mjs:436-447` even asserts that a "different, later Prompt" merges into the earlier bubble across a Question. V2's `patch()` correctly checks `last_prompt()`. V1 needs the same Prompt-closed test, or the deviation has to be written down with the owner's reason.

This builds a second copy of v2's cursors, which law 6 forbids. The brief says "Reuse V2's logic and CSS ... do not write a second version". The diff adds `.chatbox-cursor`/`.chatbox-smart-cursor` (`Chat.css:611-617`), which match `ChatV2.css:57-61` line for line, plus `cursor_mark()`, labelled "V1's own copy" in `Chat.js`. These should be one shared class and one shared element maker that both views import.
One doc is now stale. `ux/Dictate/doc/notes.md:762` still says the bubble chat "draws it as a single ✓ while `fast` is set ... (`sent_badge` in `ext/Chat/Chat.js`)". This diff deletes `sent_badge`.

A fresh agent couldn't pick this up from the task folder. `requirements.md` has no row for either ask this diff builds (the open bubble stays last, and V1's two cursors), and `plan.md`'s round-4 next steps don't mention them. Neither brief has a result or report file. The comment in `Chat.js` `tracked_text_node()` points at a "`v1-cursors` task report" that doesn't exist. The brief also asked for a 400 px and a 1200 px screenshot. Neither is in `shots/` or `chat-live/shots/`: the only `bubbles-400-*` frames there are from earlier rounds, and there's no 1200 frame at all.

The colours don't match the brief. It asks for "green when the fast seat placed it" and "pink when smart finalized or answered". The code colours both on `sent.*` (the code comment says so), and the smart cursor uses `var(--warn)`, not pink. The comment's explanation is fair (there is no per-piece placed or answered signal yet), but that gap belongs in `requirements.md` as an open item.

Nothing in production calls `fast_chunks()` in `ext/Chat/chunks.js`; only `chunks.test.mjs` uses it. The fast cursor always sits at the end of the text, so the readme line calling it "the shared splitter" overstates its role. Either drop it or use it when the cursor moves to the newest chunk (finding 1).

`last_finished_sentence_end()` finds the sentence with `text.lastIndexOf(last)`. That lands too late if the unfinished tail repeats the last sentence word for word, for example "Yes. And yes. And yes." followed by more words. This is rare. Adding up the lengths of the split sentences would be exact.

`open_bubbles` holds on to a bubble even after it leaves the DOM. A merge into it then runs `$box.el.append(last)`, which re-attaches it (`Chat.js` `speak()` and `chat()`). If anything ever clears the box without dropping the map, the old bubble would come back. Checking `last.isConnected` in `mergeable()` would close this.

findings.text: V2 does not move an answered Question to the newest end of the thread, which is what the owner asked for (ask 12 and the brief: "below newer cards"). `ext/Chat/v2/ChatV2.js` `move_to_end()` only moves the card to the end of the container it is already in. A Question whose `from` names a Prompt lives in that Prompt's nest, so it stays above every newer Prompt. V1 (`ux/Dictate/Widget.js` `show_task`) moves the card to the end of the whole `$bubbles` list. The two chats now behave differently.

V2's live order and its order after a reload disagree, and V1 and V2 follow two different rules, which breaks the brief's "ONE rule shared by V1 and V2" (law 6). `ChatV2Model.ordered()` (`ChatV2Model.js` ~L107) puts every answered Question after everything in its list, including cards that arrived after the answer. So on reload, an answered root Question from hours ago sits below every later Prompt for good. Live, the card moves once and newer cards still land below it. V1's replay puts the card where its answer landed in time. The fix is to order by the answer's time: an answered Question sorts by `answer.at`, or by its line position in the log, the same way in both chats.

The behaviour is wired in three places (`ordered()` in `children()`/`roots()`, `move_to_end` in `apply_one`, and the `moved` flag in `chat.js`), so turning it off means three edits. One static switch, for example `ChatV2Model.RESURFACE = true`, read by all three, would match the ask.
